questions.stem: A cable laying takes 2 years of work. The trench reinstatement after it may start only 1 full year after the cable work is finished. In a model with start-year variables, what is the least number of years from the cable's start to the reinstatement's start?

options.text: 1 year, the lag exactly as the engineers gave it
options.says: That reads a finish-to-start lag as start-to-start, the reading that let P023 start under P022's work.

options.text: 2 years, the length of the cable work alone
options.says: That is the finish-to-start conversion with lag 0; the year of waiting comes on top.

options.text: 4 years, the work and the lag plus one more
options.says: A parent started in year s is finished at the end of s + 1 here, so s + 2 + 1 is already the year after the waiting year.

options.text: 3 years, the length of the work plus the lag
options.says: Right: finish-to-start with lag L is start-to-start with lag d + L, here 2 + 1.

origin.section: A Lag Is Measured Between Two Events; Convert Every Lag to Start-to-Start

questions.stem: A discretionary child C must start at least 2 years after its parent P and, if both are funded, at most 1 year after it. Both projects have long windows. What does the solve return?

options.text: OPTIMAL, with C started 1 year after P when both are funded
options.says: One year breaks the minimum of 2; no pair of start years meets both lags.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with C never funded, whatever P does
options.says: Right: with a minimum above the maximum, C has no usable year, and the plan simply leaves it out, as with P023 at max lag 0.

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since no pair of years meets both lags
options.says: The rows hold with C at 0, so the model has plans; only a check reports the crossed lags.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with C started 2 years after P, the minimum
options.says: The maximum row refuses 2 years when both are funded; no row is dropped in favour of another.

origin.section: A Minimum and a Maximum Lag Make a Window Between Two Projects

questions.stem: Parent P may start in 2027 to 2030 and its child C in 2028 to 2031, with a start-to-start lag of at least 2 years and no maximum. C is discretionary. Which start variables can be deleted before the model is built?

options.text: C's 2028 and P's 2030, the years without a partner
options.says: P may be funded without C, so P's 2030 stays; parent years go only when the child must be funded.

options.text: Only P's 2030, the year that no C start can follow
options.says: P in 2030 is a valid plan on its own; it is C's 2028 that can never be 1.

options.text: Only C's 2028, the year that no P start can serve
options.says: Right: C in 2028 would need P by 2026, outside P's window; a discretionary child's partner years stay.

options.text: None of them, since the lag rows refuse every one
options.says: The rows refuse C in 2028 in every plan, which is exactly why its variable can go before the solve.

origin.section: Lags Shrink Windows Before the Solve
